test_title: PYST 32: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 22 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following human activities contributes the most to the increase in atmospheric carbon dioxide levels?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Burning of fossil fuels**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **burning of fossil fuels** such as coal, oil, and natural gas is the primary contributor to the increase in **atmospheric carbon dioxide levels**.
 
• This process releases **carbon dioxide (CO₂)** and other greenhouse gases into the atmosphere, which trap heat and contribute to global warming.
 
• Fossil fuels are burned for various purposes, including **energy production**, transportation, industrial processes, and electricity generation.
 
• The use of fossil fuels has increased significantly since the **Industrial Revolution**, causing a rapid rise in atmospheric CO₂ levels.
 
• This activity accounts for the largest share of **anthropogenic (human-caused) emissions** globally. Hence, this is the correct option.
 
• Other human activities mentioned in the options, such as construction of dams, use of fertilizers, and afforestation, have a lesser impact on atmospheric CO₂ levels compared to the burning of fossil fuels. Afforestation, in fact, helps reduce CO₂ levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fossil Fuels:**

 
 
• **Coal, oil, and natural gas** are the most widely used fossil fuels.
 
• They are formed from the remains of plants and animals that lived millions of years ago.
 
• Fossil fuels are considered non-renewable resources because they take millions of years to form.
 
• **Countries like China, the United States, and India** are among the largest consumers of fossil fuels for energy production.
 
 
 
• **Greenhouse Effect:**
 
 
• The burning of fossil fuels releases greenhouse gases such as **carbon dioxide (CO₂)**, methane (CH₄), and nitrous oxide (N₂O).
 
• These gases trap heat within the atmosphere, leading to **global warming** and climate change.
 
• The concentration of CO₂ in the atmosphere has increased from about **280 ppm (parts per million)** before the Industrial Revolution to over **400 ppm** today.
 
 
 
• **Other Human Activities:**
 
 
• **Construction of dams**: Dams impact ecosystems but do not directly contribute significantly to CO₂ emissions.
 
• **Use of fertilizers:** Fertilizers release nitrous oxide, another greenhouse gas, but their contribution to CO₂ emissions is lower.
 
• **Afforestation:** Planting trees absorbs CO₂ from the atmosphere, helping to mitigate climate change rather than contributing to it.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Data:**

 
 
• According to the **Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC)**, fossil fuels contribute about **75% of global greenhouse gas emissions**.
 
• The **Paris Agreement (2015)** aims to limit global temperature rise by reducing the use of fossil fuels and shifting to renewable energy sources.
 
 
 
• **Renewable Energy:**
 
 
• Transitioning to renewable energy sources such as **solar, wind, and hydroelectric power** can significantly reduce CO₂ emissions.
 
• Many countries, including **Germany and Sweden**, are leading efforts to adopt clean energy technologies.
